newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore computer industry calm over 2000 bug.
newsitem.headline: Singapore computer industry calm over 2000 bug.

text.p: The Singapore computer industry is concerned about the millenium bug threatening the world's computers in 2000, but is not overly anxious about it, officials of an industry group said on Tuesday.

A survey by the Singapore Federation of the Computer Industry (SFCI) showed that the number of organisations aware of the problem ranged from a high of 75 percent in the finance sector to only 33 percent in communications.
"I think most people are concerned about it, but it may not be as high as in Europe or the United States," SFCI chairman William Liu told reporters.
"We know the year 2000 will be bad for a lot of organisations," SFCI official Darke Sani added. "The bigger the company, the more affected they are."

Many computer systems use a two-digit number in denoting a year. When the year 2000 rolls around, the computer will read "00" as "1900" and this may play havoc with everything from bank statements to air traffic control systems.
The cost of debugging computer systems affected by the date change could take years and cost millions of dollars, computers experts say.

The SFCI said 54 percent of the 323 respondents in its survey planned to modify their programmes while the remaining 46 percent would modify or discard software or switch to new computer applications.
About two-thirds of Singapore computer companies plan to tap external resources to tackle the 2000 computer bug, it said.
